context_candidates.text: After decades of progress, global extreme poverty is projected to rise That poverty is now concentrated in economies where progress has stalled has profound implications for the outlook on extreme poverty. Because the population is also growing most rapidly in these same economies, the rising share of the global population in these economies is pulling the global poverty rate upward, even if national rates do not worsen. The stalled reduction in poverty may not merely be a temporary setback.6 If per capita growth in these economies continues at the pace observed over 2015–24, the global extreme poverty rate and the number of people living in extreme poverty will increase by 2030 (refer to figure 1.9). This would represent an unprecedented reversal of the decades-long decline in the global number of the extreme poor.

metadata.section: Gains in global poverty reduction could be reversed in coming decades

context_candidates.text: Poverty rates in many low-income economies, particularly those in a fragile and conflict- affected situation, are projected to decline only marginally.8 These same economies are projected to experience substantial population growth (refer to figure 1.10).9 Thus, it is the growing population in economies with high poverty rates, not the rising poverty rates, that give these economies greater weight in the aggregate poverty rate and that is driving the projections of rising global poverty rates. Fragile economies that are involved in conflict are at the center of this pattern. Economies such as the Central African Republic, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Mozambique, Niger, Sudan, and the Federal Republic of Somalia combine some of the highest current poverty rates with some of the most rapid projected population growth.

context_candidates.text: The societal poverty line, a relative measure of poverty, was developed to capture the shifting nature of deprivation across income levels. Following the recommendations of the Atkinson Commission on Global Poverty (World Bank 2017), the societal poverty line varies according to the living standards in an economy. It is set equal to $1.30, plus half the median consumption or income in the economy, with a floor at the $3.00 international poverty line (Foster et al. 2025) (refer to annex 1A). This (weakly) relative approach reflects a recognition that poverty partly involves exclusion from a normal life in a given society. It also allows the poverty line to be specific to an economy. Eighteen percent of children under the age of 18 are living in extreme poverty, compared with 6 percent among adults, and individuals with no formal education have a poverty rate of 22 percent. Extreme poverty rates in rural areas are more than three times higher than urban rates. Although extreme poverty declined across most demographic groups between 2013 and 2023, progress was slowest among households caring for children in which none or only one working-age adult was working. • Subnational data reveal that poverty is concentrated not only in specific economies, but in specific regions within these economies. metadata.section: Poverty persists unevenly across people and places
Gains in global poverty reduction could be reversed in coming decades

answer: Chưa đủ bằng chứng trong kho để trả lời. Các đoạn tìm được (trang 44 và 74 của báo cáo Poverty, Prosperity, and Planet 2026) chỉ cho thấy người nghèo tập trung ở nông thôn, ít học, trẻ em và hộ có ít người trong độ tuổi lao động làm việc; tỷ lệ nghèo cùng cực ở nông thôn cao hơn thành thị hơn ba lần; và giảm nghèo cùng cực 2013–2023 chậm nhất ở hộ có trẻ em mà không có hoặc chỉ có một người trong độ tuổi lao động làm việc. Tuy nhiên, không có đoạn nào nêu dự báo tăng trưởng nông nghiệp năm 2026 hay giải thích cơ chế nông nghiệp tăng trưởng thấp làm chậm giảm nghèo. Không suy diễn thêm từ kiến thức ngoài kho.
